bio.en: Sander Schulhoff is the OG prompt engineer - creator of the first prompt-engineering guide on the internet - who partnered with OpenAI on the first and largest AI red-teaming competition, HackAPrompt, and now works with frontier labs on model security.
bio.zh: Sander Schulhoff 是“元老级提示工程师（OG prompt engineer）”——互联网上第一份提示工程指南的创作者——他曾与 OpenAI 合作发起首个也是规模最大的 AI 红队竞赛 HackAPrompt，如今与前缘实验室合作研究模型安全。

summary.en: Sander explains how prompt engineering actually works and how his thinking has evolved, sharing lessons from building the first prompt-engineering guide and running HackAPrompt. He discusses the future of AI agents, why red-teaming and security matter more as models get more capable, and practical habits for getting dramatically better results from LLMs. The episode changed how Lenny himself uses large language models.

turns.speaker: Sander Schulhoff
turns.en: I guess implicitly it's, is this a positive or negative review? turns.en: Sure. Role prompting is really just when you give the AI you're using some kind of role. So you might tell it, "Oh, you are a math professor," and then you give it a math problem. turns.speaker: Sander Schulhoff

turns.speaker: Lenny Rachitsky

turns.speaker: Sander Schulhoff

turns.speaker: Sander Schulhoff
turns.en: ... I ended up being right. And a couple months later, one of the researchers who was involved with that thread, who had written one of these original analytical papers, sent me a new paper they had written, and was like, "Hey, we re-ran the analyses on some new data sets and you're right. There's no effect, no predictable effect of these roles." And so my thinking on this is that at some point with the GPT-3, early ChatGPT models, it might've been true that giving these roles provides a performance boost on accuracy-based tasks, but right now, it doesn't help at all. turns.speaker: Sander Schulhoff
turns.en: So decomposition is another really, really effective technique. So instead you give it this task and you say, "Hey, don't answer this." Before answering it, tell me what are some subproblems that would need to be solved first? And then it gives you a list of subproblems. And honestly, this can help you think through the thing as well, which is half the power a lot of the time. And then you can ask it to solve each of those subproblems one by one and then use that information to solve the main overall problem.
